pairs.subject: self-healing
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/AiDiagnosisCard.tsx:82 The context's only path from a diagnosis to a fix is copying a prompt to the clipboard for a person to run, so no machine applies a change on its own diagnosis and the self-healing precondition does not hold; searching the evaluator directory for rollback, remediat, healer, selfHeal and revert found nothing, and the crash libs (src/lib/crash-analyzer, src/lib/crash-health) contain no automated healer either.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/AiDiagnosisCard.tsx:82 The fix goes to the clipboard, and from there a person decides what to run. Nothing here mutates anything automatically, so there is no surface to bound.

src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/AiDiagnosisCard.tsx:162 The UI asks the person to check the prompt before running it. No change is applied by machine, so there is nothing to watch or roll back.
src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/AiDiagnosisCard.tsx:146 One fix prompt per diagnosis is shown, and nothing runs it. No strategy tree picks among remediations.

src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/NoDiagnosisNotice.tsx:52 The context does a diagnosis-like job well: it matches signatures, marks strong vs weak matches, and has an honest 'no diagnosis' lane. But all of it feeds a person, never a healer, so the technique's healer-facing precondition does not hold.

src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/index.tsx:309 Crashes are grouped into signature patterns so a person can triage them. No healer gives up and promotes an incident, so the futility and dedup rules for healer incidents do not apply.
